blocks.text: ISTANBUL, Turkey — Turkish police on Tuesday detained dozens protesting against a nationwide LGBTQ crackdown that the government says is intended to protect traditional family values, AFP journalists at the scene reported. The protesters had gathered outside Istanbul’s main Caglayan courthouse under heavy police surveillance, chanting, “Long live the struggle for freedom!”, “Free those detained immediately!” and “Despite hatred, long live life!” The demonstration followed sweeping police raids in several cities, including Istanbul and the capital Ankara, at the weekend, in which police arrested dozens of people as part of what the government says is President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s “Decade of […]...
